blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A depot model maximizes deliveries as its primary objective at the default priority, and adds an auxiliary objective that minimizes fuel with priority 5. Which plan does a hierarchical solver return?

options.text: The least-fuel plan, since priority 5 outranks priority 0
options.says: Objectives go from the lowest number to the highest, so deliveries (priority 0) come first.

options.text: A plan trading deliveries against fuel at five to one
options.says: A priority is an order, not a weight; 5 and 1 would rank the same way.

options.text: A plan chosen for fuel alone, since the primary objective is ignored
options.says: The primary objective takes part like any other, at its priority, which is 0 by default.

options.text: The most-deliveries plan, and among those the least fuel
options.says: Right: priority 0 goes first, and the fuel objective only chooses among plans with the best deliveries (with no tolerance set).

origin.section: Each Objective Has a Priority, and the Lowest Number Goes First

questions.stem: An objective is maximized first and reaches 4,000. Its ObjectiveParameters set an absolute tolerance of 30 and a relative tolerance of 0.5%. What may later objectives let it fall to?

options.text: 3,950, since the two allowed losses add up to 50
options.says: The tolerances do not add: a value within either one is accepted, so the larger single loss applies.

options.text: 3,980, since the relative tolerance takes precedence over the absolute
options.says: Neither takes precedence: 0.5% of 4,000 is 20, the absolute tolerance is 30, and meeting either one is enough, so 30 applies.

options.text: 3,970, since the larger of the two allowed losses applies
options.says: Right: the allowed losses are 30 and 0.5% of 4,000 = 20; meeting either is enough, so the loss is 30 and the floor 3,970.

options.text: 4,000, since the first objective must keep its best value
options.says: That is the case with no tolerance; these tolerances exist so that it can fall.

origin.section: A Tolerance Lets a Later Objective Buy Something From an Earlier One

questions.stem: A colleague adds an auxiliary objective to a MathOpt model and wants it solved in the course's runner with OR-Tools 9.15. What works?

options.text: Solving each objective in turn, keeping each within its tolerance
options.says: Right: that is the hierarchical method itself, and any MIP solver in the runner can run each step.

options.text: Sending the model to SCIP, since SCIP is the solver that takes indicators
options.says: SCIP refuses it: 'SCIP does not support multiple objectives'.

options.text: Sending the model to CP-SAT, since CP-SAT can take several objectives
options.says: CP-SAT refuses it too: 'CP-SAT does not support multiple objectives'.

options.text: Sending the model to HiGHS, since it reads the objectives in order
options.says: HiGHS refuses it: 'Highs does not support multiple objectives'.

origin.section: No Solver in the Runner Takes Auxiliary Objectives
